subject: Request: temporary SLO adjustment for weekly batch peaks
messages:
From: Amir Patel <amir.patel@maplehealth.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: natasha@maplehealth.com, procurement@maplehealth.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 14:05:12 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary SLO adjustment for weekly batch peaks

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Maple Health is excited about the integration. We ran a short pilot and hit a consistent pattern: our nightly bulk ingestion (03:00–04:30 PT, weekly on Tuesdays) creates a sustained burst of short calls that pushes a percentage of requests into the p95 tail for the hosted API. This is our batch job that writes clinical-event metadata and triggers a series of small prompt calls.

We'd like to request a temporary, scoped SLO exception for that 90-minute window (two consecutive Tuesdays to start) so we can complete rollout without false-positive SLO violations in your telemetry. Specifically:
- Request: exclude the 03:00–04:30 PT weekly ingestion window from p95 breach calculations for two weeks while we optimize batching on our side.
- Volume: ~18k requests during the window (avg 200/sec peak).
- Impact: outside the window, traffic matches your normal p50/p95 profile.

If needed we can provide a short recording, the job config, and SOC2 docs (attached). What's the fastest path to formalize this in the contract/monitoring?

Appreciate it — Amir
Amir Patel
Lead Platform Engineer, Maple Health
amir.patel@maplehealth.com

Attachments: maple_slo_request_summary.pdf, supplychain_SOC2_v3.pdf
From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Amir Patel <amir.patel@maplehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 16:18:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLO adjustment for weekly batch peaks

Hi Amir — thanks for the clear summary and for attaching the SOC2. This is the kind of specificity that helps us evaluate exceptions quickly. Quick notes and next steps from our side: 

- We can consider a scoped measurement carveout for a defined maintenance-like window, but we need to validate:
  * exact recurrence (you said weekly Tuesdays 03:00–04:30 PT)
  * whether the requests are concentrated to a single route/model or spread across several endpoints
  * peak qps and whether the traffic is uniformly bursty vs short-sustained calls

- Proposal: trial 2-week carveout starting next Tuesday. During that window:
  1) We mark those timestamps as scheduled-exception in our monitoring (will be excluded from p95 calculation for the purpose of SLA reporting).
  2) We run a joint engineering sync to attempt lightweight client-side optimizations (batching aggregation) — Karthik can outline low-effort changes.
  3) If we see sustained degradation in other windows or customer impact, we reserve right to abort and revert.

Marissa, Karthik — looping you in for product/ops sign-off. Lauren, FYI on the potential contract addendum.

Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0173

Attachment references: maple_slo_request_summary.pdf
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, Amir Patel <amir.patel@maplehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:02:19 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLO adjustment for weekly batch peaks

Hi all — technical context from SRE/runtime: I reviewed the draft request and attached a one-page checklist we use for SLO exceptions (see attached slo_exception_checklist.xlsx). A few items to call out: 

- p50/p95 measurement: our hosted API computes percentiles on a rolling 30-day window with per-region aggregation. SLA reporting strips scheduled exceptions when explicitly registered and tagged; this will remove the window from the SLA math but not from raw tracing.

- Important: we need to narrow scope by route and region. If the ingestion traffic hits multiple regions we either require per-region carveouts or a short-term routing change so traffic originates from a single region during the window.

- Alternatives to carveout we can propose immediately:
  * Temporary routing to a dedicated pool during the window (reserved capacity nights) — reduces noisy neighbors but has cost implications.
  * Enable aggressive prefix/KV caching for repeated prompt contexts — often cuts p95 substantially.

- Risk controls: let's put automated rollback rules and a 24/7 on-call during the trial nights. If p50 drops >10% in other windows or error-rate >0.5% we abort and re-evaluate.

If Maple can confirm route names and region and share a short sample trace of the spike, we can schedule the exception registration by EOD Friday.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachments: slo_exception_checklist.xlsx
From: Amir Patel <amir.patel@maplehealth.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, procurement@maplehealth.com
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 08:14:36 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLO adjustment for weekly batch peaks

Camila / Karthik — thanks, all. We confirm:
- Recurrence: Tuesdays 03:00–04:30 PT for the next two weeks (June 29 and July 6).
- Route: /v1/generate-clinical-metadata (proxied from our ingestion cluster, us-west-2).
- Peak qps: max observed ~220/s, sustained ~160/s for 12–15 minutes inside the window; remainder are intermittent spikes.
- Trace sample: attached in the PDF (maple_slo_request_summary.pdf).

Procurement (procurement@maplehealth.com) is looped for contract addendum — what language do you need? We can accept the scoped carveout in reporting but need the alteration reflected in the monthly SLA appendix and a brief note in the PSR that the two-week period is excluded from breach calculations.

We appreciate the rollback controls and will have an engineer on-call both nights. Please go ahead and register the exception if Marissa/legal signs off.

Thanks — Amir

Attachments: maple_slo_request_summary.pdf, supplychain_SOC2_v3.pdf
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Amir Patel <amir.patel@maplehealth.com>, procurement@maplehealth.com
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:22:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLO adjustment for weekly batch peaks

LGTM from product. I'll approve the two-week exclusion for reporting only. Lauren — can your team draft a one-paragraph SLA addendum: scope (route + region + timestamps), dates, and rollback conditions (as Karthik called out)? Once procurement confirms language we can attach and close.

Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
